Fixed. `[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)` now gives `

[foo bar](/uri)

`, which matches commonmark.js and markdown-it. The full spec suite passes (1781 pass, 0 fail), the unit tests pass (190 pass, 0 fail), and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. **Cause:** In `src/Tokenizer.ts`, the shared `outputLink` helper (used for both inline and reference links) turned the link text into tokens and always wrapped them in a link. It never checked whether the text already contained a link. It also cleared `state.inLink` to `false` when it finished instead of putting back the earlier value. So an image inside link text switched the flag off for the rest of the outer link's text, and a bare URL after the image could still be auto-linked inside it. **Fix:** - **`src/Tokenizer.ts`:** A counter goes up each time a bracketed link is created. `outputLink` compares the counter before and after reading the link text. If it changed, the text contained a link, so the outer link is dropped: it returns just a literal `[` and parsing carries on, letting the inner link win as CommonMark 6.3 requires. - This also covers deeper cases, such as a link containing an image that contains a link. - Images are still allowed to contain links (CommonMark allows that). - `` autolinks don't count as nested links, because the CommonMark reference implementation doesn't treat them that way. - `outputLink` now restores the earlier `inLink` value instead of setting it to `false`. - `Tokenizer.link()` can now return a `Tokens.Text`, as `reflink()` already could. This changes the method's public return type. - **`src/Lexer.ts`:** The inline link branch now merges that literal `[` into the text before it, the same way the reflink branch already does. **Results:** - `[foo [bar](/uri)][ref]` now gives `[foo bar]ref`. That is spec example 532's expected output; the bug report's summary line ending in `](/uri)` only applies to the first input. - Example 519, `[foo *[bar [baz](/uri)](/uri)*](/uri)`, now matches the spec. **Tests:** I didn't add a new unit test. Instead, I removed the `"shouldFail": true` flag from examples 518, 519 and 532 in both `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`, so the spec suite now checks them as passing tests.
